mokha.name: Mokha
mokha.summary: A Red Sea port city in Yemen that was the principal port for Yemen's capital and, from the 16th to 19th centuries, the world's main marketplace for coffee, giving its name to 'mocha'.

aden.name: Aden
aden.summary: Ancient port city on Yemen's south coast, at the eastern approach to the Red Sea, serving since 2014 as the de facto capital of Yemen's internationally recognized government.

hodeidah.name: Hodeidah
hodeidah.summary: The fourth-largest city in Yemen and its main port on the Red Sea, with a population of about 735,000 as of 2023.

jeddah.name: Jeddah
jeddah.summary: The largest city in Mecca Province and Saudi Arabia's main commercial center, on the Red Sea coast; it grew prominent from 647 CE as the chief port for pilgrims traveling to Mecca.

berbera.name: Berbera
berbera.summary: A coastal port city in Somaliland, once a major trading hub on the Somali seaboard and later capital of British Somaliland from 1884 to 1941.

hejaz.name: Hejaz
hejaz.summary: A historical region of western Arabia, in modern Saudi Arabia, containing the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, the first and second holiest sites in Islam.

first-saudi-state.name: First Saudi State
first-saudi-state.summary: Arabian polity from 1744 to 1818, also called the Emirate of Diriyah, founded by an alliance between Muhammad bin Saud and religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab.

al-baqi-cemetery.name: Al-Baqi Cemetery
al-baqi-cemetery.summary: The oldest Islamic cemetery in Medina, holding the graves of Muhammad's family and companions, whose tombs and domes were demolished by Wahhabi forces in 1806 and again in 1926.

ijazah.name: Ijazah
ijazah.summary: A license authorizing someone to teach a text or subject, especially Islamic religious knowledge, granted by a holder of that same authority; some scholars link it to the origin of academic degrees.

muhammad.name: Muhammad
muhammad.summary: The founder of Islam, born around 570 CE in Mecca, whom Muslims believe received revelations from God beginning around 610 as the final prophet.

jannat-al-mu-alla.name: Jannat al-Mu'alla
jannat-al-mu-alla.summary: Historic cemetery near Mecca's Masjid al-Haram, believed to hold the graves of several relatives and companions of the prophet Muhammad.

khadija-bint-khuwaylid.name: Khadija bint Khuwaylid
khadija-bint-khuwaylid.summary: The first wife of the Islamic prophet Muhammad (c. 554–619), a wealthy Meccan merchant and the first person credited with converting to Islam.

fatima.name: Fatima
fatima.summary: Daughter of the Islamic prophet Muhammad and his wife Khadija, and wife of Ali; revered by Muslims, especially Shia, as a model of piety and compassion.

house-of-saud.name: House of Saud
house-of-saud.summary: The ruling royal family of Saudi Arabia, descended from Muhammad bin Saud, founder of the 18th-century Emirate of Diriyah, and today among the wealthiest families in the world.

rashidi-dynasty.name: Rashidi dynasty
rashidi-dynasty.summary: Arabian dynasty (1836–1921) that ruled the Emirate of Ha'il and was the House of Saud's fiercest rival, until defeated by Abdulaziz Al Saud in 1921.

karbala.name: Karbala
karbala.summary: A major city in Iraq and a holy site of Shia Islam, where Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, was killed by Umayyad forces in 680 CE; it later became a major pilgrimage destination.

wahhabism.name: Wahhabism
wahhabism.summary: A Salafi revivalist movement within Sunni Islam named after the 18th-century scholar Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, originating in Najd and later spreading across the Arabian Peninsula.

abdulaziz-bin-muhammad-al-saud.name: Abdulaziz bin Muhammad Al Saud
abdulaziz-bin-muhammad-al-saud.summary: Second ruler of the Emirate of Diriyah, reigning 1765–1803, son of its founder Muhammad bin Saud and son-in-law of Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab; nicknamed the 'savior of his time.'

najd.name: Najd
najd.summary: A historical central region of the Arabian Peninsula, home to about a third of Saudi Arabia's population and to the House of Saud.

ottoman-wahhabi-war.name: Ottoman–Saudi War (1811–1818)
ottoman-wahhabi-war.summary: War fought from 1811 to 1818 between the Ottoman Empire, its vassal Egypt, and the Wahhabi Emirate of Diriyah, ending with the destruction of that first Saudi state.

muhammad-ali-dynasty.name: Muhammad Ali dynasty
muhammad-ali-dynasty.summary: The ruling house of Egypt and Sudan from the 19th to the mid-20th century, named after its founder Muhammad Ali Pasha.

abdullah-bin-saud-al-saud.name: Abdullah bin Saud Al Saud
abdullah-bin-saud-al-saud.summary: Last ruler of the First Saudi State, reigning 1814–1818, executed in Istanbul by the Ottomans after their conquest ended his rule.

al-ahsa-oasis.name: Al-Ahsa Oasis
al-ahsa-oasis.summary: An oasis and historical region in eastern Saudi Arabia made up of four cities, including Al-Hofuf and Al-Mubarraz, and 22 villages.

qatif.name: Qatif
qatif.summary: One of the oldest settlements in Arabia, with a history dating to 3500 BC, historically known to the Sumerians as Dilmun and now part of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province.

al-qasimi.name: Al Qasimi
al-qasimi.summary: An Arab dynasty ruling Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah in the UAE, once rivals of Oman at sea, branded 'pirates' by the British, who raided them in 1809 and 1819.

general-maritime-treaty-of-1820.name: General Maritime Treaty of 1820
general-maritime-treaty-of-1820.summary: An 1820 treaty between Britain and Gulf rulers to suppress piracy, which led to the British protectorate over the Trucial States that lasted until the UAE's independence in 1971.

piracy-in-the-persian-gulf.name: Pirate Coast
piracy-in-the-persian-gulf.summary: A stretch of Arabian coast from modern Qatar to Oman known for naval raids against shipping until the early 19th century, later renamed the Trucial Coast.

turki-bin-abdullah-al-saud-1755-1834.name: Turki bin Abdullah Al Saud
turki-bin-abdullah-al-saud-1755-1834.summary: Founder of the Emirate of Najd, also called the Second Saudi State, which he ruled from 1823 until his death in 1834 after a period of Ottoman administration.

bani-khalid-tribe.name: Bani Khalid
bani-khalid-tribe.summary: An Arab tribal confederation that ruled southern Iraq, Kuwait and Eastern Arabia from the 15th to 18th century, later under Ottoman protection.

ajman-tribe.name: Ajman tribe
ajman-tribe.summary: A tribal confederation of the Arabian Peninsula, with members spread across Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.

mutayr.name: Mutayr
mutayr.summary: An Arab Bedouin Sunni Muslim tribe originating near Medina, later spread across central Arabia to Kuwait and southern Iraq; traditionally nomadic camel herders considered among the 'noble' tribes.

battle-of-mesaimeer.name: Battle of Mesaimeer
battle-of-mesaimeer.summary: A June 1851 three-day battle near Qatar in which Qatari forces under Mohammed bin Thani and Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani repelled an invasion by Faisal bin Turki of Nejd.

mohammed-bin-thani.name: Mohammed bin Thani
mohammed-bin-thani.summary: First ruler from the House of Thani to govern the whole Qatari Peninsula, recognized by the British in 1868; father of Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani, who later founded Qatar.

house-of-thani.name: Al Thani
house-of-thani.summary: The ruling family of Qatar, tracing its origins to the Banu Tamim tribe, currently led by Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani as a constitutional monarchy.

house-of-khalifa.name: Al Khalifa
house-of-khalifa.summary: The ruling family of the Kingdom of Bahrain, of the Anizah tribe, who conquered Bahrain in 1783; its current head is King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa.

qatari-bahraini-war.name: Qatari–Bahraini War
qatari-bahraini-war.summary: An 1867 to 1868 conflict pitting Bahrain and Abu Dhabi against Qatar, ended by a British-mediated truce that recognized Qatar's independence under the Al-Thani family.

ibn-saud.name: Ibn Saud
ibn-saud.summary: Najdi war leader and statesman who founded Saudi Arabia, reigning as king from 1932 until his death in 1953; he had ruled parts of the region since retaking Riyadh in 1902.

samuel-austin-artist.name: Samuel Austin
samuel-austin-artist.summary: An English watercolour painter (1796–1834) known especially for coastal scenes with boats and figures.

duba-saudi-arabia.name: Duba
duba-saudi-arabia.summary: A small city and governorate on Saudi Arabia's northern Red Sea coast, in Tabuk Province.

letitia-elizabeth-landon.name: Letitia Elizabeth Landon
letitia-elizabeth-landon.summary: English poet and novelist (1802-1838), known by her initials L.E.L., whose work influenced Victorian poets like the Brownings and Tennyson but was largely dismissed after her death over her perceived immorality.

rakan-bin-hithlain.name: Rakan bin Hithlain
rakan-bin-hithlain.summary: Arabian prince, poet and warrior (c. 1814–1892) who led the Ajman tribe from 1859 and was imprisoned in Ottoman Serbia during the Serbian–Ottoman Wars.

jildiyyah-mountain.name: Jildiyyah Mountain
jildiyyah-mountain.summary: A 1,107-metre mountain in Saudi Arabia noted in Arab poetry and history for its ancient petroglyphs and its role as a landmark for pilgrims.

charles-montagu-doughty.name: Charles Montagu Doughty
charles-montagu-doughty.summary: British poet, writer and explorer (1843–1926) best known for his 1888 travel book Travels in Arabia Deserta.

anne-blunt-15th-baroness-wentworth.name: Anne Blunt
anne-blunt-15th-baroness-wentworth.summary: English co-founder, with her husband poet Wilfrid Blunt, of the Crabbet Arabian Stud, who from the late 1870s traveled through Arabia buying Arabian horses from Bedouin princes.

abdul-hamid-ii.name: Abdul Hamid II
abdul-hamid-ii.summary: 34th sultan of the Ottoman Empire (1876–1909), the last to hold effective control over the fracturing state, who suspended the constitution in 1878 and ruled with absolute power.

hejaz-railway.name: Hejaz railway
hejaz-railway.summary: A narrow-gauge railway built by the Ottoman Empire from 1900, running from Damascus to Medina with a branch to Haifa, meant to link Istanbul with the Islamic holy cities.

prophet-s-mosque.name: Prophet's Mosque
prophet-s-mosque.summary: The second mosque built by Muhammad, in Medina, and the second holiest site in Islam after Mecca's Masjid al-Haram, originally serving as a community center, court, and school.

osman-nuri-pasha.name: Osman Nuri Pasha
osman-nuri-pasha.summary: Ottoman field marshal (1832–1900), also known as Gazi Osman Pasha, celebrated for holding the town of Plevna for five months against superior Russo-Romanian forces in 1877.

ziraat-bank.name: Ziraat Bank
ziraat-bank.summary: A Turkish public bank founded in 1863 that provides commercial loans alongside personal loans such as consumer, vehicle and housing loans.

sharifate-of-mecca.name: Sharifate of Mecca
sharifate-of-mecca.summary: A semi-sovereign state ruled by the Sharif of Mecca from about 967 to 1916, also called the Emirate of Mecca, which then became the Kingdom of Hejaz.

tanzimat.name: Tanzimat
tanzimat.summary: A period of reforms in the Ottoman Empire from 1839 to 1876 that modernized legal, military and administrative systems.

ottoman-land-code-of-1858.name: Ottoman Tapu
ottoman-land-code-of-1858.summary: An 1858 Ottoman land reform law that began a systematic registration programme during the Tanzimat period, followed by an 1873 land emancipation act.

muhammad-ali-of-egypt.name: Muhammad Ali of Egypt
muhammad-ali-of-egypt.summary: An Ottoman governor of Albanian origin who became de facto ruler of Egypt from 1805 to 1848, widely considered the founder of modern Egypt.

second-saudi-state.name: Second Saudi state
second-saudi-state.summary: A Saudi-ruled state in central Arabia from 1824 to 1891, restoring Saudi rule after the first Saudi state's fall, marked by less expansion and religious zeal, ending with internal conflict.

emirate-of-jabal-shammar.name: Jabal Shammar
emirate-of-jabal-shammar.summary: A state in the northern Arabian Peninsula centered on Ha'il, ruled by the Rashidi dynasty from the mid-19th century until 1921, covering parts of modern Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Jordan.

battle-of-mulayda.name: Battle of Mulayda
battle-of-mulayda.summary: The last major battle of the Second Saudi State, fought 21 January 1891, after which the Rashidis forced the House of Saud's Abdul Rahman bin Faisal and his allies to flee.

abdul-rahman-bin-faisal-al-saud-1850-192.name: Abdul Rahman bin Faisal Al Saud
abdul-rahman-bin-faisal-al-saud-1850-192.summary: Last emir of Nejd, reigning 1875–1876 and 1889–1891, youngest son of Emir Faisal and father of Abdulaziz, founder of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
abdul-rahman-bin-faisal-al-saud-1850-192.source_title: Abdul Rahman bin Faisal Al Saud (1850–1928)

muhammad-ibn-abd-al-wahhab.name: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab
muhammad-ibn-abd-al-wahhab.summary: Arab Muslim scholar and preacher (1703–1792) from Najd who called for a return to the Quran and Hadith over traditional interpretation and is considered the founder of the Wahhabi movement.

sultan-bin-bajad-al-otaybi.name: Sultan bin Bajad al-Otaybi
sultan-bin-bajad-al-otaybi.summary: Sheikh of the Otaibah tribe and Ikhwan leader (1876–1932) whose tribal army helped King Abdulaziz unify Saudi Arabia before he later rebelled and was defeated.

faisal-al-duwaish.name: Faisal al-Duwaish
faisal-al-duwaish.summary: Chief of Arabia's Mutayr tribe and a leader of the Ikhwan tribal army who helped Abdulaziz unify Saudi Arabia in the early 20th century.

arab-revolt.name: Arab Revolt
arab-revolt.summary: An armed uprising begun in 1916 by Hashemite-led Arabs against the Ottoman Empire during World War I, aiming for an independent Arab state from Aleppo to Aden.

asir.name: Asir
asir.summary: A province in southern Saudi Arabia bordering Yemen, with Abha as its capital and a population of about 2 million.

abha.name: Abha
abha.summary: Capital of Asir Province in Saudi Arabia, set about 2,270 metres up in the Asir Mountains, known for its mild climate and popularity as a tourist destination.

muhammad-ibn-ali-al-idrisi.name: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi
muhammad-ibn-ali-al-idrisi.summary: Founder and first ruler of the Idrisid Emirate of Asir, living from 1876 to 1924.

emirate-of-asir.name: Emirate of Asir
emirate-of-asir.summary: A state on Arabia's Red Sea coast founded in 1907 by Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi in revolt against the Ottomans, which expanded after World War I before being absorbed into Saudi Arabia in 1934.

johann-ludwig-burckhardt.name: Johann Ludwig Burckhardt
johann-ludwig-burckhardt.summary: Swiss traveller and Orientalist (1784–1817) who explored Arabia under the alias Sheikh Ibrahim Ibn Abdallah, and is best known for rediscovering the ruins of Petra and the temples of Abu Simbel.

age-of-revolution.name: Age of Revolution
age-of-revolution.summary: The period from the late 18th to mid-19th century marked by revolutions across Europe and the Americas that replaced absolutist monarchies with constitutional governments, starting with the American Revolution.

takfir.name: Takfir
takfir.summary: The Islamic practice of declaring another Muslim an apostate; traditionally restricted to religious scholars because of its severe, sometimes deadly, consequences.

fitna-word.name: Fitna
fitna-word.summary: An Arabic term for temptation, trial or civil strife, used in Islamic historiography for civil wars within the Muslim community, starting with the First Fitna.

ibn-taymiyya.name: Ibn Taymiyya
ibn-taymiyya.summary: A Sunni Muslim scholar and jurist (1263–1328) born in Harran, whose creedal treatises later became a key reference for the Salafi movement, despite being censored and imprisoned in his lifetime.

richard-francis-burton.name: Richard Francis Burton
richard-francis-burton.summary: British explorer, scholar and army officer (1821–1890) who spoke up to 29 languages, searched for the source of the Nile, made a disguised pilgrimage to Mecca, translated One Thousand and One Nights, and published the Kama Sutra in English.

hermann-burchardt.name: Hermann Burchardt
hermann-burchardt.summary: German explorer and photographer (1857–1909) known for his black-and-white photographic essays of Arabia in the early 20th century.
